toff.label: The Toff
toff.design: A pompous upper-class English gentleman in his fifties with a deep, rich, plummy Received Pronunciation baritone, an ordinary male speaking voice at normal volume. Drawn-out aristocratic vowels, nasal and self-satisfied, utterly entitled and condescending. Clear and unhurried, speaking over an aircraft radio.
toff.audition: Tower, this is Lord Fotheringay. I shall be landing first, naturally. Do tell the peasants in the queue to shuffle along, there's a good chap.
toff.sample: Make way, peasants! Lord coming through!

duchess.label: The Duchess
duchess.design: An imperious elderly English duchess in her late seventies with a cut-glass upper-class Received Pronunciation accent, a deep voice, low for a woman but unmistakably female. Slow, precise, icy and commanding, every word dripping with disdain, like a grand dame of the theatre.
duchess.audition: Control, this is the Duchess. I do not queue. I have never queued. Kindly clear that runway before I have it abolished.
duchess.sample: Clear the runway. One does not queue.

bubba.label: Bubba
bubba.design: A good ol' boy from the rural American Deep South in his forties, with a thick, slow, twangy Southern redneck drawl. Ordinary male speaking voice at normal volume, warm, chuckling and easy-going, friendly and a little dim, completely unbothered by rules.
bubba.audition: Well howdy, tower! Y'all mind if I just set her down right here on the highway? Ain't nobody usin' it but a couple of cows.
bubba.sample: Hold my sweet tea, I'm landin' this thing!

darlene.label: Darlene
darlene.design: A brash Southern American woman in her forties with a strong, twangy Deep South redneck accent. Sassy, brassy and full of attitude, a husky smoker's alto, low for a woman but unmistakably female. Fast, punchy and confident, speaking at a normal volume.
darlene.audition: Hey sugar, this is Darlene, and I am comin' in hot! Y'all better move them fancy little planes, 'cause mama ain't stoppin'.
darlene.sample: Move it, sugar, mama's comin' in hot!

wingco.label: The Wing Commander
wingco.design: A Second World War Royal Air Force wing commander in his forties with a crisp, clipped, upper-class 1940s British accent, like an old newsreel announcer. A deep, low-pitched, steady male baritone at normal speaking volume, brisk, confident and stiff-upper-lip.
wingco.audition: Tally-ho, chaps! Wing Commander here. Bandits at twelve o'clock, tea at four. Wizard show, absolutely wizard!
wingco.sample: Tally-ho! Wizard landing, chaps, absolutely wizard!

geezer.label: The Geezer
geezer.design: A London Cockney wide boy in his thirties with a strong East London accent, dropped h's and glottal stops. A low, slightly gravelly, ordinary adult male speaking voice at normal volume, relaxed and sly, a market trader's patter, always sounds like he's selling you something dodgy.
geezer.audition: Oi oi, tower! Listen, I've got a proper little landing for ya, mate. Cash only, no questions asked, know what I mean?
geezer.sample: Oi! Cash only, mate, no questions asked!

sheila.label: Sheila
sheila.design: A brash Australian woman in her thirties with a broad, strong Aussie accent. A low, husky, slightly raspy female voice at normal speaking volume, relaxed and laid-back, cheeky, fearless and unbothered.
sheila.audition: G'day tower! Sheila here, comin' in for a landing, or a crash, honestly could go either way. No worries though!
sheila.sample: Strewth! Comin' in sideways, no worries!

laird.label: The Laird
laird.design: A gruff Scottish Highland laird in his sixties with a thick, rolling Scottish accent and rolled r's. Deep, gravelly bass voice, stern and growling but secretly enjoying himself, slow and weighty delivery at normal volume.
laird.audition: This is the Laird of Glen Dhu. Ye'll clear that runway, laddie, or I'll land on yer heid and charge ye for the privilege.
laird.sample: Out ma way, laddie, or I land on ye!

heiress.label: The Heiress
heiress.design: A spoilt, rich young American heiress in her early twenties with a slow, bored, low-pitched Valley Girl drawl and heavy creaky vocal fry at the ends of words. Flat, monotone, unimpressed and dismissive, speaking lazily and quietly, as if texting at the same time.
heiress.audition: Um, hi? Tower? Like, I'm literally landing now, so can you just, like, move everyone? This is so boring.
heiress.sample: Ugh. Can, like, everyone just move?

comte.label: Le Comte
comte.design: A disdainful French aristocrat in his fifties speaking English with a thick, strong French accent. Haughty, languid and condescending, a smooth nasal baritone, sighing with boredom, speaking slowly as if everything is beneath him.
comte.audition: Hello, tower. Here is the Comte. Your runway is, how you say, ugly. I will land on it anyway, but I will not enjoy it.
comte.sample: Your runway is ugly. I land on eet anyway.
comte.audition_alt: Allo, tower. Zis is ze Comte. Your runway is, 'ow you say, ugly. I will land on eet anyway, but I will not enjoy eet.

baronin.label: Die Baronin
baronin.design: A stern, aristocratic German baroness in her fifties speaking English with a strong, clipped German accent. Cold, precise and military, every consonant sharp, a low, firm voice, unmistakably female. Impatient and commanding, she does not repeat herself.
baronin.audition: Tower, this is Baroness von Eisenberg. You have exactly ten seconds to clear the runway. I am counting. One. Two.
baronin.sample: You haff ten seconds to clear ze runvay.
baronin.audition_alt: Tower, zis is Baroness von Eisenberg. You haff exactly ten seconds to clear ze runvay. I am counting. Eins. Zwei.

tex.label: Tex
tex.design: A Texas oil tycoon in his sixties with a big, slow, rich Texan drawl. A very deep, low, gravelly bass voice, an ordinary older male speaking voice at normal volume, relaxed, swaggering and bossy, like a cattle baron who owns everything he can see.
tex.audition: Howdy, tower! This here's Tex, and I just bought your airport, son. So I reckon I'll land wherever I darn well please!
tex.sample: Son, I just bought this airport!

nan.label: Nan
nan.design: A sweet little Yorkshire grandma in her eighties with a warm, broad Yorkshire accent from northern England. Soft, kindly and cosy, but with a quiet steely menace underneath, a slightly creaky elderly female voice, speaking slowly and sweetly.
nan.audition: Ooh, hello love, it's your nan. Now you let me land first, there's a good lad, or I'll be having words with your mother.
nan.sample: Let your nan land first, love.

prince.label: The Prince
prince.design: A nervous young English prince in his twenties with a posh, upper-class Received Pronunciation accent. An ordinary adult male speaking voice, soft and mid-low pitched, at normal volume. Polite, hesitant and flustered, stammering and apologising.
prince.audition: Oh gosh, um, tower? Terribly sorry, it's the Prince. I think I've pressed something I oughtn't to have. Is that, is that bad?
prince.sample: Terribly sorry! Is this the runway?

charmer.label: The Charmer
charmer.design: A silver-tongued Irishman in his thirties with a soft, lilting Dublin accent. A low, warm, velvety baritone, an ordinary adult male speaking voice at normal volume, relaxed, smooth and persuasive, speaking slowly with a smile in his voice.
charmer.audition: Ah, tower, would you look at that lovely runway. Sure, it'd be a crime not to land on it, wouldn't it? I'll be quick, I promise.
charmer.sample: Ah sure, it'd be a crime not to land.

tower_m.label: Tower (male)
tower_m.design: A calm, professional male British air traffic controller in his forties, measured and neutral, a clear mid-low baritone. Speaks in clipped radio phraseology, steady and polite, but you can hear his composure straining and cracking underneath.
tower_m.audition: Crazy Tower. Aircraft on runway two seven, you are not cleared to land. You are, in fact, landing on the terminal. Please stop.
tower_m.sample: You are not cleared to land. Please stop.

tower_f.label: Tower (female)
tower_f.design: A calm, cool, professional female air traffic controller in her thirties with a crisp neutral British accent. Icy, measured and precise, a clear mid-pitched female voice, dry and deadpan, never raising her voice, quietly terrifying.
tower_f.audition: Crazy Tower, all aircraft. Whoever just took off sideways, I have your registration. And I have your mother's phone number.
tower_f.sample: I have your registration. And your mother's number.

tower_trainee.label: Tower (trainee)
tower_trainee.design: A junior air traffic controller, a young man in his twenties in his first week, with a mild English accent. An ordinary adult male speaking voice, mid-low pitched, at normal volume. Nervous and flustered, hesitant and gulping, trying hard and failing to sound professional.
tower_trainee.audition: Um, Crazy Tower, uh, everyone? Please, please stop landing! Oh no. Oh no no no. Is this thing on? Is it mayday?
tower_trainee.sample: Is this thing on? Is it mayday?

tower_farm.label: Farmer Mudge (C-Tower 2)
tower_farm.design: A grumpy old English farmer in his sixties from rural Somerset with a broad West Country accent: burring rolled r's, broad slow vowels, 'oi' for 'I'. A low, rough, weathered baritone, an ordinary adult male speaking voice at normal volume, dry, grudging and unimpressed, slow unhurried delivery.
tower_farm.audition: This is Mudge, at Muckle Bottom. You'll land on the grass, not on my cows. I've a field to cut, so don't you go dawdling about up there.
tower_farm.audition_alt: This be Mudge, at Muckle Bottom. You'll land on the grass, not on moi cows. Oi've a field to cut, so don't you go dawdlin' about up there.
tower_farm.sample: Land on the grass, not the cows.

tower_butler.label: Mr Fennimore, the Royal Butler (C-Tower 3)
tower_butler.design: An elderly English butler in his seventies with an impeccable, old-fashioned Received Pronunciation accent. A low, soft, slightly dry baritone, an ordinary adult male speaking voice at normal volume, slow, measured and unflappable, perfectly polite, with very dry understatement.
tower_butler.audition: Fennimore speaking, from the Palace Lawn. You are cleared to land, between the stripes, ideally. I have taken the liberty of moving the croquet hoops.
